paper.title: Online Market Making and the Value of Observing the Order Book

settings.name_in_paper: Online market making with order book access, stochastic independent market prices
unmapped: Online market making: learner posts bid b < ask a in [0,1]; reward 1(V<=b)(M-b)+1(a<=V)(a-M)
Action-dependent feedback: trader valuation V_t observed only if no trade (B_t<V_t<A_t); market price M_t always observed
Valuations V_t i.i.d. from unknown c.d.f. F with no smoothness assumption; market prices M_t independent with common mean mu (not necessarily identically distributed), independent of V_t
settings.definition_quote: At the end of the round, if $\boxed{B_t< V_t< A_t}$ the agent observes $V_t,M_t$, otherwise only $M_t$. ... The evaluations $M_t$ are an independent sequence with mean $\mu$.

settings.name_in_paper: Online market making with order book access, local mean reversion (AR(k) market prices)
unmapped: Online market making: bid/ask pair in [0,1], reward 1(V<=b)(M-b)+1(a<=V)(a-M)
Action-dependent feedback: V_t observed only if no trade; M_t always observed

Market price follows AR(k) process M_{t+1}=sum gamma_tau M_{t-tau}+(1-gamma) eta_{t+1}, E[eta|F_t]=mu, sum gamma_tau = gamma<1 (exogenous, not affected by learner); environment 'markovian' used only to signal temporal dependence of the price process
Valuations V_t i.i.d. from unknown c.d.f. F
settings.definition_quote: For some arbitrary initial conditions $\{M_t\}_{t=-\tau}^0\subset [0,1]$, the market price evolves according to the following $AR(k)$ process: $M_{t+1}=\sum_{\tau=0}^{k-1}\gamma_\tau M_{t-\tau}+(1-\gamma)\eta_{t+1}$ ...

settings.name_in_paper: Online market making with order book access, global mean reversion
unmapped: Online market making: bid/ask pair in [0,1], reward 1(V<=b)(M-b)+1(a<=V)(a-M)
Action-dependent feedback: V_t observed only if no trade; M_t always observed
Market price satisfies global mean reversion: E[X_{t+1}|F_t]*S_t <= 0 with X_t=M_t-mu, S_t cumulative deviation (exogenous dependent process); 'markovian' used only to signal temporal dependence
Valuations V_t i.i.d. from unknown c.d.f. F
settings.definition_quote: There is some constant $\mu$ such that, given $X_t:=M_t-\mu$ and $S_t=\sum_{\tau=1}^tX_\tau,$ one has, for every $t\le T$ $\E[X_{t+1}|\Fs_t]\cdot S_t\le 0.$

settings.name_in_paper: Online market making with order book access, adversarial (oblivious) market values
unmapped: Online market making: bid/ask pair in [0,1], reward 1(V<=b)(M-b)+1(a<=V)(a-M)
Action-dependent feedback: V_t observed only if no trade; M_t always observed
Valuations V_t remain i.i.d. from unknown c.d.f. F (stochastic), only market prices M_t are an arbitrary oblivious sequence in [0,1]
settings.definition_quote: in this section, we focus on the case where no assumption is put on $M_t$, which is allowed to be any sequence of values in $[0,1]$.

conditions: holds on the complement of failure event E, which has probability at most 2*delta

source.label: thm:regstoc
source.quote: Under Assumptions \ref{ass:bounded} and \ref{ass:order}. Under $E^c$ (the failure event in \Cref{eq:failure}), the pseudo-regret suffered by \Cref{alg:OPSR} is bounded by $\Rs_T\le\sqrt T+2 + 4\sum_{t=1}^{T-1} \psi(t,\delta)+\phi(t,\delta)$ which, for $\phi,\psi$ as in Equations \eqref{eq:mu_ci} and \eqref{eq:bid_ci}, writes as $$\Rs_T\le \sqrt{48T\log(3T/\delta)}+\Os\left(\sqrt{T\log (\log (T))}\right).$$

results.notes: Leading term exact, lower-order term O(.). Pseudo-regret defined via J(b,a)=F(b)(mu-b)+S(a)(a-mu). Probability is 1-2delta. Per-step complexity O(sqrt T). Theorem holds conditional on event E^c, which uses the stochastic market price assumption.

source.label: thm:regstoc
source.quote: By \Cref{thm:regstoc}, \Cref{prop:ecdf}, and \Cref{prop:stoch_reg}, for \Cref{alg:OPSR} we have, with probability at least $1-\delta$, $$R_T\le \sqrt{48T\log(9T/\delta)}+\Os\left(\sqrt{T\log (\log (T))}\right).$$

results.notes: Stated in text after the theorem, not a separate formal statement. R_T is regret vs best fixed (b,a) in hindsight w.r.t. realized M_t, expectation over V_t only.

symbols.gamma_ar: sum of AR coefficients gamma = sum_tau gamma_tau < 1
symbols.k_ar: order k of the AR(k) price process

conditions: M_t follows AR(k) process with nonnegative coefficients summing to gamma<1 and innovations in [0,1] with conditional mean mu (Assumption 5)

source.label: thm:regretmr
source.quote: Under Assumptions \ref{ass:bounded}, \ref{ass:stoch_val}, \ref{ass:order} and one between \ref{ass:ou_mar} and \ref{ass:mr_mar}, the regret suffered by \textsc{LazyOPSR} is bounded, with probability at least $1-\delta$, by $$R_T\le \begin{cases} \sqrt{2007\cdot T\log(6T/\delta)}+\frac{8\gamma (k+1)\log(T)}{(1-\gamma)}+\Os(\sqrt T)&\text{under \Cref{ass:ou_mar}}\\ \sqrt{20783\cdot T\log(6T/\delta)}+\Os(\sqrt T) &\text{under \Cref{ass:mr_mar}} \end{cases}$$

results.notes: Explicit leading terms with O(sqrt T) remainder; notation O for whole expression. Paper also gives pseudo-regret bounds for OPSR under these assumptions in text (not recorded).

source.label: thm:regretmr
source.quote: Under Assumptions \ref{ass:bounded}, \ref{ass:stoch_val}, \ref{ass:order} and one between \ref{ass:ou_mar} and \ref{ass:mr_mar}, the regret suffered by \textsc{LazyOPSR} is bounded, with probability at least $1-\delta$, by ... \sqrt{20783\cdot T\log(6T/\delta)}+\Os(\sqrt T) under \Cref{ass:mr_mar}

conditions: M_t any oblivious sequence (cannot depend on the perturbation epsilon)
tuning: perturbation epsilon ~ Unif(0, T^(-1/2)) added to the mean price estimate

source.label: thm:regradv
source.quote: Under Assumptions \ref{ass:bounded}, \ref{ass:stoch_val} and \ref{ass:order} and let $\{M_t\}_{t=1}^T$ be any unkown oblivious sequence. For $\kappa=\left \lceil \log(3T)^{\frac{1}{3}}T^{\frac{2}{3}}\right \rceil$, the regret suffered by \Cref{alg:ETP} is bounded, in expectation, by $$\E[R_T]\le 5\log(T)^{\frac{1}{3}}T^{\frac{2}{3}}+\Os\left(\sqrt T \log(T)\right).$$

results.notes: Proof ends with log(3T) instead of log(T) in leading term; recorded as stated in theorem. Regret is expectation over V_t and the algorithm's randomization against the best fixed pair in hindsight.
